newsitem.title: USA: Rainforest Cafe secure on FY97 estimates.
newsitem.headline: Rainforest Cafe secure on FY97 estimates.

text.p: Rainforest Cafe Inc said Monday it is confident it will meet earnings estimates of $0.80 per share for fiscal 1997 in spite of reports an analyst lowered his estimate and a 14 percent share price decline.

"To my knowledge only one of the analysts (that covers company) has lowered his estimate for fiscal 1997," Mark Robinow, the company's chief financial officer, said in an interview. "The company remains confident with a previous consensus estimate of $0.80 per share (for fiscal 1997)."
Robinow said the company does not comment on daily changes in its stock price, but he added that there have been no news announcements or any changes in what he called "our business fundamentals."

The company's shares closed down 3-3/8 at 20-5/8 Monday after an analyst at Wessels, Arnold & Henderson LLC lowered his estimate for the company's fiscal 1997 earnings, said Robert Evans, an analyst at John G. Kinnard & Co.
"The stock is probably down because analysts are lowering the fiscal 1997 earnings estimate because of slippage in (the company's) development level for 1997," Evans said.
Last fall the Minneapolis-based company, which operates a chain of six themed restaurants, announced plans to open six U.S. restaurants and two eateries in Cancun and London in 1997.

Mark Bartholomay, an analyst at Dain Bosworth, said Wessels, Arnold analyst David Garrity actually confirmed a fiscal 1997 estimate of $0.74 a share and raised the estimate for 1998 to $1.18 from $1.13.
Garrity did not return calls to confirm the figures.
In the third quarter ended September 29, Rainforest Cafe reported earnings of $1.9 million, or $0.13 per share, on revenues of $15.7 million.
For fiscal 1996, which ended December 31, Dain Bosworth's Bartholomay estimates earnings of $0.38 per share.
The company expects to report fourth-quarter results in early February, Robinow said.

The Motley Fool, a financial services site on America Online, said Monday that Wessels believes Rainforest Cafe's same-store sales in the fourth quarter at its Mall of America flagship restaurant would be flat because of a decline in the overall retail environment.
Rainforest Cafe declined to comment on the Motley Fool report.

Bartholomay said Montgomery Securities reported last month that Rainforest Cafe's comparable store sales would be about two percent lower than in 1995. The company declined to comment on same-store sales in the period.
Last week, Bartholomay revised his 1997 estimate to $0.76 from $0.83 and his 1998 estimate to $1.35 from $1.30.

"The company announced in December that it was pushing back the openings of two units to 1998 from 1997," he said, "but it also moved up the opening of another unit in Chicago near the third quarter (of 1997 from 1998)."

A Rainforest Cafe spokeswoman confirmed that the opening of a second restaurant in the Chicago area will be moved up into 1997 and the opening of two other units will now take place in 1998 instead of this year.
